text:
From the identity $1+{cot}^{2}⁡\theta ={csc}^{2}⁡\theta ,$ with $\theta =5x-2,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}1+{cot}^{2}⁡(5x-2)={csc}^{2}⁡(5x-2).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into our integral gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{{cot}^{2}⁡(5x-2)\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x-2)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x-2)}\,\text{d}x & = \\ \int \frac{1}{[{cot}^{2}⁡(5x-2)+1]\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x-2)}\,\text{d}x & = \\ \int \frac{1}{{csc}^{2}⁡(5x-2)\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x-2)}\,\text{d}x & = \\ \int \frac{{sin}^{2}⁡(5x-2)}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x-2)}\,\text{d}x & = \\ \int \operatorname{sin}⁡(5x-2)\text{d}x & = \\ -\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x-2)+C & .\end{aligned}
$$
